A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 21-page versions of the same study, with corresponding main sections and Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v6 reports original CLIP/OpenCLIP bias and debiasing evaluations on FairFace and PATA, plus neutral-image controls, calibration results, and prompt-sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v7 retains these original evaluations and supplementary empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The CLIP/OpenCLIP audit procedures, contrastive objective, bias calculations, and Bias Prompts, Prompt Array, and SANER procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same FairFace/PATA evaluations, neutral-portrait control, training-data coverage, and crime/non-human, communion, and agency tasks. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same checkpoint comparators and debiasing methods participate in the corresponding comparisons in Tables 1 and 3. The related-work citation edits do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sections 3.2–3.6 and Appendices A–C retain the same sample selections, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, controls, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The neutral-image control, directional-bias calibration, and prompt-template sensitivity analyses in Appendices A–C retain the same questions, procedures, and evidence.

E5.justification: The 95% bootstrap confidence-interval reporting in Figures 1 and 4 and the appendix summary statistics are unchanged. No seed, run-count, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–10 retain the same results and findings. For example, FairFace CLIP-B/32 gender–crime skew remains 1.19 in Table 1 and 0.11 with Bias Prompts in Table 3 in both versions.

T1.justification: The contrastive-loss, Max Skew, Harm Rate, projection, and calibration mathematics are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about data source, scaling, and source- and size-dependent mitigation. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of scaling and mitigation effects remain identical, as do the limitations concerning demographic coverage, model scope, proprietary data, task selection, dataset overlap, and compute.

D1.justification: Inference settings, mitigation hyperparameters, hardware and runtime disclosures, code link and release statements, and Appendix D's exact prompt lists are unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 removes Bianchi, Nozza, and Hovy (2023) from Section 2.2 and the bibliography, leaving Liang et al. supporting the retained family–career stereotype statement. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to citations, bibliographic wording, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The MMBias entry changes author, title, and venue information; substantive prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Citation editing slightly rewraps Section 2.2 and reflows references and limitations on pages 13–15; the Chuang et al. entry moves from page 14 to page 13. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. On page 14, v7 replaces the separate MMBias entry with a duplicate of the retained Janghorbani–De Melo title and authors, but lists EMNLP instead of EACL. This introduces a localized bibliographic inconsistency, with no demonstrated compensating improvement in the supplied PDFs.
